Selected Story
The story explains the GitHub CLI documentation’s three-class categorization of Linux installation methods and what that classification means for a reader choosing how to install gh. The documentation groups installers as Recommended (official Debian/RPM/Homebrew packages and project-provided precompiled binaries, described in the docs as supported/updated by the GitHub CLI maintainers), Community (distribution- or third‑party packages the GitHub CLI team explicitly does not maintain or support), and Discouraged (methods the docs warn against, most notably Snap). The main point for readers is that the documentation treats installer options differently according to who maintains them and that those maintenance categories — not technical speculation — should guide how the choice is presented to users.

Story Progression
- Context: Linux desktop users, developers, and sysadmins need a clear, practical way to decide how to install gh. The documentation itself organizes install methods into three named classes: Recommended (Official), Community (Unofficial), and Discouraged; it also states which package types the project maintains and which it does not.
- Development: Make concrete what each class means, using only documented claims: Recommended installs (Debian/RPM/Homebrew and project precompiled binaries) are described in the docs as supported and updated via the project’s workflows; Community packages are explicitly noted as not maintained by the GitHub CLI team and are acknowledged as unsupported (illustrate this with the Arch/AUR example as a concrete case of community maintenance); the Discouraged section issues an explicit WARNING against certain methods and specifically states never to install gh as a Snap.
- Endpoint: The documentation’s central, supported insight is that installer choice should be framed by these maintenance/support classes: identify which class an available installer belongs to (Recommended, Community, or Discouraged) and present that classification to readers as the primary basis for deciding which installation path to follow.

Critical Constraints
- Do not claim or invent why the project labels an option Recommended or Discouraged beyond the documented statements about who maintains or does not maintain a package and the presence of warnings.
- Do not attribute collective decisions, motivations, or internal policies to an unspecified team beyond the documentation’s explicit references (preserve only the documented phrasing that the GitHub CLI team does or does not maintain certain packages).
- Do not assert specific levels, scope, or SLAs of support for “supported” packages; limit wording to the documentation’s statement that those packages are supported/updated by the project.
- Do not explain or invent technical causes for Snap problems; the docs link to issues but do not document the root causes on the install page.
- Do not reproduce exhaustive install commands or enumerate every community package list; use a single concrete example (Arch/AUR) if an illustration is needed.
